name: AgentMod
author: Kadim Gültekin

sections.description:
AgentMod is an AI Agent Platform built natively for WordPress. Unlike standard AI chatbot plugins, AgentMod acts as an orchestration layer on top of the Connectors, WP AI Client infrastructure introduced in WordPress 7.0.

Instead of writing custom integration code (glue-code) for external services, AgentMod creates an Ability Economy: it reads abilities exposed by plugins like WooCommerce (create_order), Core (get_site_info), or Native Custom Fields (create_post_type) directly from the WordPress Core Registry and makes them available to AI agents — turning your site into an autonomous operating platform.

Key Features (Free Version)

AI Orchestration Engine
A stateless, model-agnostic agent engine built on the native WordPress AI Client. Supports sequential and parallel multiple ability calls via WP_AI_Client_Ability_Function_Resolver.

Admin Chat Widget
A React-based chat panel triggered from the WordPress Admin Bar. Built with @wordpress/components Modal architecture. Includes a “New Topic” button to reset the session and conversation history at any time.

Context Scope Selector
A toggle control inside the chat composer that lets the user decide whether the AI agent can read site data or should operate on general knowledge only.

Search & Content Tools
– Search queries return a maximum of 20 post titles/excerpts per call.
– Full content processing is limited to a maximum of 5 post bodies at once. Requests like “Analyze all 500 posts” are gracefully declined.
– A maximum of 10 ability calls are allowed per message cycle.

Write Action Confirmation Modal
When an agent triggers a database-modifying ability such as create_post or send_email, an approval modal is shown to the user with a summary of the action. The operation is not executed until the user explicitly confirms.

Smart Response Rendering
– Plain text responses are rendered as Markdown with “Copy Text” and “Create Draft” action buttons.
– Code block responses (HTML, CSS, PHP, etc.) are displayed in a syntax-highlighted <pre> container with a “Copy Code” button.

Site Management Abilities
A group of abilities that let the agent administer the WordPress installation itself, covering the same ground as the wp plugin, wp theme, wp option, wp user, wp core and wp cron command families — without needing shell access or WP-CLI:
– Plugins and themes: list, look up, search the WordPress.org directory, install from a slug or a .zip, activate, deactivate, update and delete.
– Settings: browse WordPress’ registered settings with their declared types, and update them with schema validation. Individual options can be read and written too.
– System: report the WordPress, PHP and MySQL versions, pending updates and whether the site permits file modifications; list scheduled cron events; flush the object cache and rewrite rules.
– Users: list accounts, create users, edit profiles, change roles, send password resets and delete accounts with content reassignment.

Every destructive or state-changing ability in this group goes through the approval modal, and guards refuse the operations that would break the site: writing siteurl, deactivating AgentMod itself, deleting the active theme, removing the last administrator or the account you are signed in as. Passwords are never generated into a response — WordPress sends its standard emails instead.

Ability Registry Browser
A dedicated sub-menu page under AgentMod lists all abilities currently registered on WordPress Core Registry, with detailed information for each.

Secure System Directives
The PromptBuilder enforces strict system-level directives that prevent agents from performing destructive actions and require them to ask clarifying questions in ambiguous situations.

Developer Hook System
A comprehensive set of PHP and JavaScript hooks for extending AgentMod:
– Filters for prompt modification (before/after)
– Actions for ability execution lifecycle (before/after)
– ChatPanel UI customization hooks (add/remove tools, sections)

Get Pro to Unlock More Features

Unlock advanced features and take your AI Agents to the next level.

  • AgentMod Hub: Browse and import ready-to-use agents, skills, and more from a public hub, no manual setup required.
  • Multi-Agent System: Create and manage multiple specialized AI agents, each with its own role and personality.
  • Agent Tray: Switch between your AI agents right from the chat interface.
  • Conversation History: Automatically save, search, and restore past conversations.
  • Additional Abilities: Unlock 40+ extra abilities for your agents to work with.
  • AI Skills: Attach reusable, custom skills to your agents.
  • Full-Screen Workspace: A dedicated, distraction-free environment to manage every AI feature in one place.
  • Scheduled Tasks: Build multi-step scheduled agent runs and make your website act autonomously.
  • Frontend Widgets: Add AI-powered widgets to your site, such as contact forms or FAQ floating chat panels.
  • Code Snippets: Save, manage, and run code snippets alongside your AI agents.
  • Import / Export Tools: Export and import settings, custom fields, and plugin configuration.

Provider Agnostic

AgentMod does not lock you into any specific AI provider. It works with any provider supported by the WordPress AI Client, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and others configured via provider plugins.

Requirements

  • WordPress 7.0 or higher (requires native WP AI Client & Abilities API)
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • An active AI provider plugin compatible with WordPress AI Client

Credits

Built using official WordPress packages:

  • @wordpress/scripts
  • @wordpress/components
  • @wordpress/elements
  • @wordpress/icons
  • @wordpress/data

Assets:

  • All images located in the Admin/assets/img folder are self created and are licensed under CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication.

Composer Packages:

  • PHP DI – Copyright (c) Matthieu Napoli

Libraries:

  • Native Custom Fields – Copyright (c) Arkenon (https://wordpress.org/plugins/native-custom-fields/)

Source Code

It is available on GitHub:
* GitHub: https://github.com/Arkenon/agent-mod

Developers

If you want to contribute to the plugin:
1) Download the source code and run npm install to install the development dependencies.
2) To install composer dependencies, run composer install.
3) Run npm start to start the development server.
4) To build the plugin, run npm run build.
sections.faq:
Who is this plugin for?

AgentMod is designed for WordPress site owners, developers, and agencies who want to leverage AI agents to automate tasks on their site using the native WordPress Abilities API — without writing custom integration code for each service.

Does AgentMod work with any AI provider?

Yes. AgentMod is fully provider agnostic. It uses the native WordPress AI Client layer, so any AI provider plugin compatible with WordPress 7.0’s AI infrastructure will work.

What is an “Ability” in this context?

An Ability is a registered, callable action exposed by a WordPress plugin through the Core Abilities Registry. For example, WooCommerce might expose a create_order ability, or a booking plugin might expose book_appointment. AgentMod reads these automatically and makes them available to the AI agent.

Can the AI agent delete my content?

No. Destructive actions (delete, erase, trash) are strictly prohibited by system-level directives in AgentMod’s PromptBuilder. The agent will never execute a delete operation directly. Any write or modifying action additionally requires explicit user confirmation via an approval modal before it is executed.

Is there a limit on how much content the AI can read?

Yes, hard limits are enforced to manage performance and token costs:
– Search results: maximum 20 titles/excerpts per query
– Full content reading: maximum 5 post bodies per cycle
– Ability calls per message: maximum 10

Where can I see which Abilities are available?

Under the AgentMod menu in your WordPress admin, there is a dedicated Abilities sub-page that lists all abilities currently registered in the WordPress Core Registry, along with their details and parameters.

What happens if I want to create a post via the agent?

If you ask the agent to create a post, it will show you a confirmation modal summarizing the action before anything is written to the database. You must explicitly approve the action for it to proceed.
sections.changelog:
1.3.4

  • Added: Dynamic tool loading, the new default. Instead of sending every ability with every request, the agent starts with a few tools and loads the abilities a task needs through the new agent-mod/find-abilities tool; what it finds stays available for the rest of the run, and tools used in the recent messages are loaded up front. On a site with about 100 abilities, the tool definitions sent with each request drop from about 23,000 to about 1,100 tokens, so even a “hello” costs a fraction of what it did. Write confirmation, auto-approval and the read-only rule of Ask and Plan modes work exactly as before. Agents with 15 or fewer abilities still get all of them up front. The new “Tool Loading” setting (Settings > Abilities) switches back to sending every ability.
  • Changed: The “Ability Source” and “Allowed Abilities” settings are removed. The default agent can use every ability and finds the ones it needs; a selection saved in an earlier version is no longer applied.
  • Changed: AgentMod’s own chat tools (ask-user, present-plan, request-approval, find-abilities) moved to a separate “AgentMod — System” ability category. They are offered automatically where they apply and are no longer part of ability selections, where selecting or leaving them out never had an effect.
  • Fixed: The MCP Adapter plugin’s abilities (discover-abilities, get-ability-info, execute-ability) are no longer offered to the agent. execute-ability could run any other ability under its own name, so the confirmation dialog showed “execute-ability” instead of the actual action, and a session approval for it covered every ability.
  • Added: create-post and update-post can assign taxonomy terms (categories, tags and custom taxonomies) with the new terms parameter, one item per taxonomy. Terms are given by ID, slug or name and replace the post’s terms in that taxonomy; an empty list removes them, and append: true on update-post adds to the existing ones. Taxonomies left out keep their terms. Missing terms are never created on the fly: the call fails and points to create-terms. The taxonomy, the post type and the user’s permission to assign terms are checked before anything is saved, and terms are set before a post is published so publish-time hooks see them. Previously the agent could create terms but had no way to attach them to a post.
  • Improved: get-post returns the post’s assigned terms, grouped by taxonomy, including the taxonomies that have none, so the agent can see what is assigned and which taxonomies it can use.
  • Improved: Older tool results are compacted only when the conversation grows large. Before, everything except the last four tool results was cut to a short stub on every step, even in a short run, so the agent lost data it had just fetched (for example a post type’s custom field configuration) and had to ask for it or fetch it again. Now nothing is compacted until the history reaches about 80,000 tokens; it is then reduced to about 40,000, and the six most recent results are always kept in full.
  • Improved: Compaction keeps the already compacted part of the history unchanged until the next compaction, so the providers’ prompt cache (OpenAI, Gemini) is reused across steps instead of being invalidated on every step.
  • Improved: A compacted nested result, such as a field configuration (sections, fields, sub-fields), keeps its structure (names, types, labels, options) instead of only its first 200 characters. The same summary is passed on to the following messages.
  • Improved: Native Custom Fields configuration reads (get-post-meta-fields, get-term-meta-fields, get-user-meta-fields, get-options-page) are never compacted, and are passed on to the following messages with a larger summary.
  • Fixed: A read-only tool whose earlier result had been compacted could not be called again, because the repeat guard counted it as an identical call. The agent then had neither the data nor a way to get it back. Such a call now runs again.
  • Fixed: With “Enable site context” on, the agent still called get-site-info and get-environment-info on every request to fetch values that were already in the site context. The site context now includes the PHP version and tells the agent to use these values directly, and the default system prompt no longer asks for a tool call when the answer is already in the site context or the conversation.

1.3.3

  • Added: Bulk text replace in posts. preview-bulk-replace (read-only) shows, for up to 100 posts at once, how many matches each post has with a before / after snippet, without saving anything. bulk-replace-content then applies the same change on the server; changed posts get a revision when their post type supports revisions. Literal text or regular expressions, an optional limit per post (e.g. only the leading label), case-insensitive matching that handles the Turkish i / ı / İ / I, and by default only the visible text is changed, never block comments or attributes. A change that would alter the block structure skips that post. Previously a task such as “remove the ‘Short bio:’ label from these 12 posts” needed a get-post and an update-post per post, and ran into the full-content read limit and the tool-call limit.
  • Improved: list-posts filters. titles finds many posts by title in one call (ignoring case, extra spaces and accents, with a “contains” fallback) and reports the titles that matched nothing. Also added: include / exclude IDs, search_columns (e.g. search titles only), content_contains / content_not_contains, meta_query with comparison operators (!=, LIKE, IN, EXISTS, NOT EXISTS, > …) and AND / OR, tax_query, author, date_after / date_before, content_preview (the start of each post’s text, which does not count against the full-content read limit) and fields: "ids" for the smallest output.
  • Fixed: In long runs the agent listed the same posts again and again. Older tool results are compacted to save context, and a post list lost its IDs after a few more tool calls; the same happened between messages (“continue”). List results now keep every ID and title when compacted.
  • Fixed: A read-only tool called again with exactly the same arguments in one run now gets a notice to reuse the earlier result, and from the third identical call on it is not executed, so a looping agent no longer uses up the tool-call limit and the provider’s token limit.
  • Fixed: list-posts passed an unchecked orderby value to the query.

1.3.2

  • Added: Navigation menu abilities. list-navigations lists the block theme’s menus (wp_navigation) with their item count and the templates / template parts that show them (e.g. the footer). get-navigation returns a menu as a tree of items addressed by path. update-navigation edits the existing menu in place with add / update / remove / move operations (a link that gets children becomes a submenu), or replaces its markup; all operations are validated before anything is saved. Previously the agent could not reliably edit an existing menu and created a new one instead.
  • Added: Approval request dialog in Execute mode with Manual approval. When the agent wants your go-ahead before acting (for example because it chose a different approach than you asked for, such as a code snippet instead of editing a plugin file, the scope grew, or a step cannot be undone), it calls its new request-approval tool. A dialog shows what it will do, with “Continue”, “Request changes” (typed right in the dialog) and “Cancel”; closing the dialog counts as Cancel. On Continue the agent carries the action out in the same run, and write actions still pass through the usual confirmation dialog. The tool is not offered in Auto mode, in Ask or Plan mode, or in unattended runs.
  • Fixed: In Manual approval mode the agent could end its turn by announcing an action (“I am preparing the snippet”) without doing it or asking, which read as if the work was done. Execute mode now tells the agent never to end a turn by announcing work it has not performed, and in Manual mode to ask for the go-ahead with the approval dialog instead of in plain text.
  • Improved: When get-post or update-post is called with the wrong post_type, the error now names the post’s actual type. Navigation menus are pointed to the navigation abilities and templates to the template abilities, instead of every mismatch being sent to the template abilities.
  • Fixed: The full-content read limit of get-post now counts distinct posts. Re-reading the same post (e.g. after its earlier result was compacted out of the history) no longer uses up the limit and locks the agent out of that post.
  • Fixed: create-post, update-post, create-pattern, update-pattern, duplicate-pattern and add-or-update-template / add-or-update-template-part stripped backslashes from the saved content. Escaped characters in block attributes (e.g. " for a quote) were lost, and a backslash in an attribute value left invalid JSON behind, so the block lost its attributes in the editor. Backslashes in titles were stripped too.
  • Improved: Error notices in the chat panel are shown right above the composer instead of at the top of the conversation, so a stopped run is noticed without scrolling up.
  • Improved: The chat modal no longer shows a second scrollbar; it uses the full height available and only the conversation scrolls. On very short screens the modal still scrolls as a fallback so the composer stays reachable.
  • Improved: The composer (presets, message field and toolbar) stays fixed at the bottom of the chat modal from the first open, as in the AI Workspace, instead of sitting right below the last message.
  • Improved: The conversation scrollbar in the chat modal and the Pro AI Workspace is thinner and light gray.
  • Fixed: Long answers typed in the question dialog or as “Request changes” in the approval dialog were cut off. The agent saw only the first 2000 characters while answering, and only about 500 characters of the answer in later messages (fewer with non-Latin characters such as Turkish letters). A long list pasted as an answer was therefore treated as a much shorter list. Answers are now kept in full for the rest of the conversation, even in long runs and in older turns. If an answer is still longer than the limit, the agent is told that it was cut off.
  • Added: “Max Answer Length (characters)” setting under Settings > AI Limits. It sets the longest answer kept from the question and approval dialogs. Default: 20000.
  • Improved: Tool results kept in the conversation history no longer store non-Latin characters as escape sequences. Text with accented letters (e.g. Turkish) now takes much less of the history space.
  • Updated: NCF library (native-custom-fields) to v1.4.6
  • Fixed: The “Details” buttons on the Abilities page were always blue. They now use the admin color scheme chosen in your profile, like the other primary buttons.

1.3.1

  • Added: The agent can ask you questions in a dialog instead of in the chat. Single-choice questions use radio buttons, multiple-choice questions use checkboxes, every question can take your own answer in a text field, and the option the agent recommends is preselected. Submitting continues the agent’s run where it stopped; “Skip” lets it continue with sensible defaults, which it names. Questions are only offered in the admin chat, never in unattended runs.
  • Added: Plan review dialog. In Plan mode the agent hands over the finished plan with its new present-plan tool; the plan stays in the conversation and a dialog offers “Approve & Execute” (with a Manual or Auto approval choice), “Ask Agent to Review”, “Request Changes” (typed right in the dialog) and “Close”. Answers to general questions in Plan mode do not open it.
  • Improved: Execute mode now tells the agent to carry the request out in the same turn instead of describing what it is about to do and stopping, and to call write tools directly, since their approval is handled by the confirmation dialog. It asks only when a missing detail would materially change the outcome.
  • Improved: In Plan mode the agent settles open choices (which fields or options to include, names and slugs, scope) with you before writing the plan, even when the request left the choice to it.
  • Improved: Ability descriptions no longer say “Requires user confirmation”, which made agents ask for permission in chat before every write. The four irreversible deletions (plugin, theme, user, term) still ask for confirmation unless you explicitly requested that deletion.
  • Improved: The default base system prompt asks before calling a tool only when that tool needs a detail you have not given and the agent cannot look up or reasonably default, instead of “before calling any tools”. Sites that saved their own prompt keep it; update it under Settings to pick up the new wording.
  • Improved: list-posts returns posts in any status (drafts included) and can filter by post_status and by a custom field (meta_key/meta_value).
  • Improved: get-post also returns the post status and its custom fields; create-post and update-post can write custom fields, and update-post can change the status (e.g. publish a draft). In update-post every field except post_id is now optional, so fields left out stay unchanged.
  • Removed: The agent-mod/list-recent-posts ability; use list-posts with orderby “date” and order “DESC”.
  • Fixed: Inline citation markers from provider web search (e.g. “citeturn1view1”) no longer show up in answers.

1.3.0

  • Added: Setup wizard. After activation (and from the “No provider” link in the chat) a full-screen wizard walks you through connecting an AI provider via WordPress Connectors, choosing the basic agent settings (role, goal, base system prompt, personality, RAG, web search, default model, preset prompts), previewing Pro features and browsing the abilities the agent can use. Every settings step can be skipped.
  • Added: Dashboard reminder to finish the setup until it is completed or dismissed.
  • Improved: The Abilities list component can now be embedded in other screens.

1.2.6

  • Added: Approval mode picker in Execute mode. “Manual” (default) keeps the confirmation dialog for every write action; “Auto” runs every tool call without asking. The choice is kept in memory only, so a page reload always falls back to Manual.
  • Improved: Live tool-call progress is now shown in a collapsible card with the running tool and a call counter in its header. Each call appears as a bordered row with its status (running/done) and a one-line argument preview, and long runs show only the latest calls until “Show earlier calls” is clicked.

  • Changed: “Upgrade to Pro” links now point to https://agentmodwp.com/pro-features/ instead of the direct Freemius checkout link.

  • Fixed: Tool calling failed with a “400 Bad Request” on Anthropic and Google when any registered ability declared an input schema those providers do not accept — for example WooCommerce 11.x product-create / product-update. Because the full tool list travels with every request, one unsupported schema broke every message, including plain chat with no ability call involved.
  • Added: Anthropic connector repair — a tool’s top-level oneOf / anyOf / allOf is flattened into a single object schema. Branch properties are merged and their enums are unioned, so no option the schema offered is lost.

  • Full-Screen Workspace: A dedicated, distraction-free environment to manage every AI feature in one place.
  • Scheduled Tasks: Build multi-step scheduled agent runs and make your website act autonomously.
  • Frontend Widgets: Add AI-powered widgets to your site, such as contact forms or FAQ floating chat panels.
  • Code Snippets: Save, manage, and run code snippets alongside your AI agents.
  • Import / Export Tools: Export and import settings, custom fields, and plugin configuration.

Provider Agnostic

AgentMod does not lock you into any specific AI provider. It works with any provider supported by the WordPress AI Client, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and others configured via provider plugins.

Requirements

  • WordPress 7.0 or higher (requires native WP AI Client & Abilities API)
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • An active AI provider plugin compatible with WordPress AI Client
